title: fix(plugin-security)!: the Layer 0 tenant write wall refuses an update that empties a row's organization
body:
Fixes #22278
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changes

`plugin-security`'s Layer 0 tenant write wall (`security-plugin.ts`, step 3.7, the tenant post-image check) judged only an organization a write *names*. A non-system update that *emptied* the row's organization was never judged, on either half of the step: the payload as sent, and the row the engine is about to store (the #20013 seam, by id and by predicate).

On UPDATE the step now holds its stated invariant whole: where the tenant wall applies, the row's organization after a non-system update is one the wall admits. An emptied organization is refused on both halves with the wall's `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (ADR-0112 envelope), and nothing is stored. The step's comment states the invariant.

- INSERT keeps today's rule: an absent or empty organization is the stamp's to fill.
- System writes, the platform-administrator posture exemption on posture-permitting objects, and the `single` posture are unchanged.
- An update that does not touch the column, or keeps the row's own organization, is unchanged.

Scope as ruled (triage `6059271770`, the seat's ruling B): one region of `security-plugin.ts`, one test file, one changeset. No `packages/spec`, no change to how `@objectstack/core` reads an organization-less grant, no change to `grant-holder-membership-refusal.ts`, nothing that widens access.

## Tests: `tenant-wall-organization-removal.test.ts`

Both SQL driver families (driver-sql on better-sqlite3, driver-sqlite-wasm), `isolated` posture unless a cell says otherwise. Refusals assert `code` and `status`, that the refusal names the object, and that the stored rows are unchanged.

- Negative pins (7 per driver): an emptied organization on both grant tables, by id and by predicate; the platform administrator on the grant tables (their posture grants no exemption); an ordinary tenant object on both update paths; the stored-row half (a value the `beforeUpdate` chain wrote) on both update paths.
- Controls (10 per driver): an untouched-column update on both grant tables and on an ordinary tenant object; a system write; an explicit foreign organization, still refused; the platform-administrator exemption on a posture-permitting object, stored-row half included; the `single` posture; an INSERT keeps its stamp.

| run | tree | result |
|---|---|---|
| before the fix (merged base, corrected controls) | `d3ec5074fb` | 12 negatives red, 20 controls green |
| with the fix | `edafba04e9` | 34 of 34 green |

### The two controls that were red on base: wrong expectation, diagnosed

"A platform administrator on a posture-permitting object is exempt" and "the `single` posture is unchanged" asserted that a caller-*sent* empty organization is stored on an ordinary tenant object. It is not, wall or no wall. There `organization_id` is the registry's injected `readonly` column, and the engine's static-readonly strip (`stripReadonlyFields`) drops a non-system caller's value before the statement; a value the hook chain wrote survives the strip. The grant tables declare the column themselves, writable, so a sent value is stored as sent.

Measured in the corrected `single`-posture control, on both drivers: the injected column reads `readonly: true` and the grant table's does not; a sent empty value is stored on the grant table and dropped on the ordinary object; a hook-written one is stored. Both controls now read each store as the engine writes it (the platform-administrator control drives the stored-row half through the hook), and are green before and after the fix.

### Ablation

One-shot, from the committed fix at `edafba04e9`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor count 1 to 0 on disk each time; every restore proven: blob equal to HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` empty). The subject is imported from source (`./security-plugin.js`), so no dist leg applies.

| mutation | red | reading |
|---|---|---|
| A1: the payload-half refusal disabled | 2 (ordinary tenant object, both drivers) | on the grant tables the stored-row half still refuses: the halves overlap there |
| A2: the stored-row-half refusal disabled | 2 (the hook-written cell, both drivers) | |
| A3: the emptied-organization predicate disabled (both halves) | 14 (all 7 negatives, both drivers); 20 controls green | |

A first A3 attempt was refused by the tool before anything ran (its anchor sat inside the replacement text); it measured nothing.
